P1.evidence: No setter notes read back despite a KFS-set call; the prospect had to volunteer that he had spoken to Kim. Frame was three-part not four — 'where are you today? Where do you want to be if we can help? I can show you one of the many options we have' — missing 'what's in the way' and 'what you need'. Agreement was a trailing 'All right?' with no pause for a yes. Open question was clean: 'I'll turn the floor over to you, Nick. How can we potentially help you?'

P2.evidence: Only work was asked: 'what do you do for work firstly?' — lineman, and the rep correctly registered it as physical. Age came out unprompted ('I'm 30') and the rep confirmed he had not asked: 'I was going to ask'. No height, no weight, no health conditions, no injury or limitation question, no diet question, no sleep question, no daytime-energy question. Shoulder and back pain, a 7:30pm bedtime and a failed calorie-counting attempt were all volunteered, never asked for.

P3.evidence: Strongest phase by far. 'What does your 10 out of 10 potential of Nick really look like?' opened the aesthetic/function picture; 'what's shifted for you recently that made you say, alright, now's the time?' bridged to motive; 'how's it going to lead into the other areas of your life?' and 'how do you show up for your girl, family?' drove outward; 'How does this influence the way we can be a father, the leader we can be' landed the legacy frame. Never asked what he wants to do physically but cannot, and the reflect-back was a want-or-need question rather than 'so this isn't really about the weight'.

P4.evidence: The phase was never run. The prospect volunteered ten years of self-taught lifting and a calorie-counting attempt that 'lasted not even a week', and named his own gap unprompted ('I just never really had anyone to like, kind of, to push me'). The rep only mirrored it back — 'you've never been challenged' — and never asked what he tried, what happened, why it didn't stick, or why he cannot stick to it alone.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame of any kind. The two-year question, the willing-to-settle question, the 'why not' and the line-in-the-sand were all absent. The closest move was 'would you ultimately say it's a want or a need to go to the next level?', which invites a label rather than making inaction cost anything — and it is the missing pressure here that let the price land against an untested urgency.

P6.evidence: A 1-10 alignment scale ran instead of the belief question — 'one is, ah, I don't need this. Ten is, I trust these guys' — and it ran after the three pillars but before price, which is the right slot; the prospect answered 'I have full trust'. The all-in question did appear, but only after the price and the payment-plan discussion: 'money aside, you want to do this, you're in?'. The rep then proceeded despite an answer that was explicitly conditional on two other conversations, rather than returning to Phase 5.

P11.evidence: An offer was presented and next steps were described, so the phase applies, but none of it executed. No payment collected, no link sent, no Trevor onboarding call booked (only described as something that would follow), no agreement email, no Skool/welcome-email/questionnaire instruction. The rep instead volunteered the delay: 'go ahead, speak to your business partner, speak to your wife'.

objection_plays.detail: Isolation ran, but late and out of order — 'money aside, you want to do this, you're in?' came after the price and after financing had already been offered, so the wallet was opened before the blocker was isolated. The 'HOW not SHOULD' reframe was absent. Permission was asked correctly ('I don't need to be in the weeds of your finances. I just need to understand things from a high level'), and cash on hand (5k), monthly bills (2.5-3k), surplus (~150-200) and credit score (~600) were collected. Not asked: number of credit cards, available credit per card, used vs available, or crypto/stocks/investments. The play was then abandoned mid-stream — instead of structuring a plan against the numbers he had just gathered, the rep proposed a follow-up call.

Trigger landed twice — 'this is obviously something that I'll have to go over with her' and 'I have to talk to John and see what other things that we're looking to kind of do'. None of the play ran: no 'money aside, do you personally feel this can get you there', no 'what obstacles might come up when you talk to her', no 'is there any reason she would not want you stronger', no ownership question, no deposit-with-refund fallback. The rep actively endorsed the deferral instead.

'If it's going to be too stressful, I might have to wait' is OD in substance, sharpened by a baby due in August and a business four months from settling. No scripted move ran. The rep went the other way: 'my intention is not to ever take food off anyone's table. You know, this is things, you can do it later.'

Script gap: a high-intent prospect who is genuinely illiquid rather than unwilling — 5k total savings, ~150-200/mo surplus, no credit card and a ~600 score, which likely fails third-party financing underwriting anyway. OC assumes recoverable credit capacity; there is no scripted path for a buyer whose constraint is real and whose financing route is probably unavailable. The rep offered Payver/Klarna without testing whether a 600 score with no credit history would be approved.

notes: Discovery was half-run: the deep-why work in P3 was genuinely strong, but Baseline, Past Attempts and the entire Consequence Frame were skipped, so the price landed with no cost-of-inaction behind it and no health picture at all. Coach on sequence — commitment check before pillars and price, and finish the financial picture you start rather than converting it into a follow-up.
